item.title: Lenskart: Complete Business Model Analysis
item.description: Lenskart, founded by Peyush Bansal in 2010, has grown into India’s leading tech-enabled eyewear brand with a vertically integrated, omni-channel model across Asia. This detailed analysis covers Lenskart’s founder journey, business strategy, financial growth, funding history, and IPO plans, highlighting its innovation, profitability, and market leadership in the global eyewear industry.

item.title: Ather Energy: Complete Business Model
item.description: Ather Energy, founded in 2013 by IIT Madras alumni Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain, has grown from a startup into India’s leading EV brand with a ₹23,601 crore market cap. Backed by Hero MotoCorp and Flipkart founders, Ather revolutionized mobility with smart scooters like the 450X and Rizta and its 4,000+ charger Ather Grid. With 17% market share, strong IPO success, and rising revenues, Ather is driving India’s sustainable electric future.

item.title: Phool.co: Complete Business Model Analysis
item.description: Phool.co, a Kanpur-based social enterprise, has revolutionized India’s temple waste management through its circular economy business model. Founded in 2017, it transforms floral waste into luxury incense, biodegradable packaging, and vegan leather (Fleather). With ₹50 crore revenue in FY2024 and over ₹106 crore in funding, Phool.co merges sustainability, innovation, and social impact, empowering women and protecting the Ganges.

item.title: The PayPal Mafia Story: When Disruption Became a Habit
item.description: The “PayPal Mafia” refers to PayPal’s early founders and employees who went on to build or invest in major tech companies like LinkedIn, YouTube, Tesla, SpaceX, Yelp, Palantir, and Affirm. Their unique culture, strong network, and shared startup experience helped shape modern Silicon Valley and drive the rise of today’s leading tech innovators.

item.title: The BlackRock HPS $500 Million Fraud: A Complete Timeline
item.description: Discover how Indian-origin entrepreneur Bankim Brahmbhatt pulled off one of the largest private credit frauds in recent years, using fake invoices, fabricated customers, and forged contracts to secure over $500 million from major lenders like BlackRock’s HPS. This detailed breakdown explains how the scheme worked, how it collapsed, and why it exposes major risks in the private credit market.

item.title: Wakefit: Complete Business Model Analysis
item.description: Wakefit IPO Analysis: Explore Wakefit’s complete business model, founding story, revenue streams, industry outlook, competitive landscape, financial performance, unit economics, valuation, risks, and growth strategy. This data-driven breakdown helps investors understand whether Wakefit is a strong long-term investment opportunity before the IPO.

item.title: The 10 biggest startup rounds of 2025 (and why they matter)
item.description: Discover the 10 biggest startup funding rounds of 2025, featuring billion-dollar investments across AI, crypto, data centers, VR, and emerging technologies. This SEO-friendly roundup breaks down who raised the most capital, key investors, global regions, and why these mega-rounds matter for venture capital, private equity, and the future of innovation worldwide.

item.title: Elon Musk: Net Worth, Empire & Origins
item.description: Elon Musk’s net worth, empire, and origins are explored to explain how SpaceX, Tesla, X, and AI ventures have made him the world’s richest entrepreneur in 2025.

item.title: CRED: Complete Business Model Analysis
item.description: CRED is a premium Indian fintech platform that rewards creditworthy users for paying credit card bills on time. This case study analyzes CRED’s business model, revenue streams, UPI growth, lending products, funding journey, and path to profitability, along with its competitive position against PhonePe, Paytm, Google Pay, Slice and OneCard in India’s fast-growing credit card and digital payments market.

item.title: Lawyered: Complete Business Model Analysis
item.description: Lawyered is an Indian legal-tech startup building legal infrastructure for the country’s mobility economy. By offering real-time roadside legal assistance and digital challan management, Lawyered shifts legal services from reactive to preventive. This article analyzes its business model, traction, funding, competitive landscape, and why it stands out in India’s evolving legal-tech ecosystem.
